25_interl2751: you help yourself, not him; whence: “for thou hast no need of my goods”
25_interl2752: neither does your justice profit him, nor does he reprove you from fear, but for your wickedness
25_marg1351: Shall he reprove for fear? Who, even out of his wits, would think that God reproves us from fear and sets his judgment against us out of dread?
25_marg1352: Shall he reprove thee for fear? Those who do not know how to measure their words slip into idle sayings.
25_marg1353: And not for thy manifold wickedness: he who did not restrain himself from idle words flared up into insulting ones. See, from a sluggish heart he came to idle words, and from idle words, through the crime of falsehood, he flared up into insults. For these are the falls of growing fault, that the tongue, when it is not restrained, by no means lies where it has fallen but always goes down to worse.
25_marg1354: For there follows: “For thou hast taken away,” and the rest that follows. These things are plain according to the letter, even if they are made up about Job. But mystically heretics are figured by them, and the Church, as we have said, by Job. The pledge, then, is the gift of the Spirit, by which we are made sure of the promises. Or the confession of sin; whence Moses: “When thy brother oweth thee any thing,” that is, when he has sinned against you, “and thou take a pledge from him,” that is, when you now hold the confession of his sin, “thou shalt restore the pledge before the going down of the sun,” that is, give back pardon for the confession before the sun of justice sets for you through grief of heart. So because the Church urges those returning from the heretics to confess the fault of their error, the heretic says: “Thou hast taken away the pledge,” etc., that is: you uselessly demand confession; or: those who come to you lose spiritual gifts.
25_interl2753: when she says: “Seek not the things that are too high for thee”
25_marg1355: And stripped the naked: he is naked who enjoys purity of heart, without the veil of doubleness; and such a one sometimes receives the doctrines of heretics, which they call clothing; but because such a one easily returns to the Church, the heretics call him naked and stripped of their garment by the Church. He is called weary who is worn out under the burden of the world; to him, they say, the Church (which they mock for its lack of skill) has not given the water of doctrine, as they who are talkative to everyone do; and they think they have not withdrawn bread while they answer boldly about things that cannot be grasped. And they believe themselves learned above all when they more unhappily presume to speak of unknown things; whereas the Church either modestly keeps silent even about things known to one whom they could not profit, or humbly confesses that she does not know unknown things and calls the curious back to the sense of ordered humility, when she says to them through her preacher: “Not to be more wise than it behoveth to be wise, but to be wise unto sobriety.” And again: “Be not highminded, but fear.” And again: “Seek not the things that are too high for thee, and search not into things above thy ability.” And again: “Thou hast found honey, eat what is sufficient for thee, lest being glutted therewith thou vomit it up.”
25_marg1356: In the strength of thy arm: as if he said: that you have occupied the land everywhere by your preaching was by power, not by the reason of truth; that is, the people believed because of the mighty of the world. In which they show that they envy the greatness of the Church.
25_marg1357: Widows: the heretics give this name to the peoples whose preachers the Church takes from them, converted or refuted; whence they also complain that the arms of their disciples are broken in pieces. Or the Church is said to break arms because she calls people back from the superstition of those who forbid to marry and condemn foods. Whence if anything adverse befalls her, they say it is repaid to her for her sins. And this is: “Therefore art thou surrounded with snares.”
25_interl2754: you who do not foresee what is to come in your striking
25_interl2755: sudden fear troubles him who does not attend to what threatens him from the judgment to come
25_marg1358: And didst thou think that thou shouldst not see darkness, etc. As if he said: you had set before yourself in hope the security of peace, and so rejoiced in your presumption, and did not reckon you would be overwhelmed by tribulations; but now in the evils you suffer it appears what kind of man you were. And see that tribulations are compared to overflowing waters, because they rush in one upon another as wave upon wave.
25_marg1359: Dost not thou think that God, etc. As if: did you think you would not be overwhelmed because you thought God does not see these lower things; and do you still think so? The heretics think themselves wise, and mock the Catholics as not fearing God because they do not see him bodily, and do not think he sees earthly things from far off because he is higher than heaven, and judges as it were hidden in a cloud through mist because there are regions of air between us and heaven, and, intent on higher things, weighs the lowest less, and while he goes round and binds the poles of heaven does not look back at the things below. But who, even out of his wits, would suspect these things of God? Who, being always almighty, so attends to all that he is present to each, and is so present to each that he is never absent from all at once? For even if he forsakes some who sin, yet he is present to those very ones by judgment from whom he is seen to be absent by help. So he surrounds the outward things as to fill the inward; so fills the inward as to surround the outward. So rules the highest as not to forsake the lowest; but is present to the lowest so as not to withdraw from the higher. So he lies hidden in his own form that yet he is known in his working. So he is known in his work that yet he cannot be grasped by the reckoning of the one who knows. So he is present that he cannot be seen; so he cannot be seen that yet his very judgments bear witness to his presence. So he offers himself to be understood by us that yet he clouds the very ray of his understanding to us; and again so holds us back with the mist of ignorance that yet he flashes on our mind with the rays of his brightness, so that, raised up, it may see something, and, beaten back, may tremble; and because it cannot see him as he is, it may know him in some measure by seeing. But the heretics do not reckon that holy Church knows these things, because by foolish judgment they think themselves alone wise. In the figure of whom it is further added: “Dost thou desire to keep the path of ages?” As the path of the Redeemer is humility, so the path of ages is pride. So wicked men tread the path of ages who walk in haughtiness through the desires of this life.
25_interl2757: as if he cannot see from so far away
25_marg1360: Who were taken away before their time: those who love the present life promise themselves longer spans of that life. But when death coming upon them takes them away, it cuts off the spans of their life which they had stretched out in thought. It must be known that God, ordering us, disposes the end too according to merits: either that the wicked man may live briefly lest he harm many; or that the good man may live longer that he may profit many; or again that the wicked man may live longer to increase the evils by which the good are tried; or that the good man may be taken away sooner lest, if he lived longer, he be corrupted by wickedness. And the sentence is changed, but not the eternal counsel.
25_marg1361: And a flood hath overthrown their foundation: the wicked, while they do not look on present things as fleeting, fix their mind in love of the present life and build in it foundations as of a long dwelling. But a flood overthrows their foundations, because the course of changeableness undermines in them the standing of their perverse building.
25_interl2760: this too he says against Job
25_interl2761: this is what Job said above: “Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him?”
25_interl2762: that they may blush at his goodness and return, and if they despise it may be punished more heavily
25_marg1362: Whereas he had filled their houses with good things: the Lord fills the houses of the wicked, because he does not deny his gifts even to the ungrateful.
25_marg1363: Whose way of thinking be far from me, etc. Job too said this above: “May the counsel of the wicked be far from me.” But counsel is in the heart, a way of thinking in the mouth. So this man wishes to be unlike Job both in the words of the wicked and in thought.
25_marg1364: The just shall see the destruction of the wicked.
25_interl2766: who here grieve over their errors
25_marg1365: And shall rejoice, when they cling to the strict judge with perfect security at last. For now they look on the reprobate and groan.
25_interl2767: because he will then look down on them exulting
25_marg1366: Is not their exaltation cut down: here the wicked are raised up, because they are lifted up by perverse actions; but their raising is cut down when they are dragged from the present life to destruction, or from the sight of the judge to Gehenna.
25_interl2769: the flesh which they leave here
25_marg1367: And hath not fire devoured the remnants of them? Because even if they leave the flesh here, they receive it back at the resurrection, so as to burn in the flesh in which they sinned.
25_interl2770: to God, which will be when you agree with me
25_marg1368: Submit thyself then to him, etc. It is a fault of pride to teach one who is better, which heretics often do to Catholics.
25_interl2772: because I will no longer quarrel against you
25_interl2775: as if what I say comes from his mouth
25_interl2776: as if he said: which until now you have had in your mouth and not in your heart
25_marg1369: If thou wilt return: because you have been torn down from the building of justice.
25_marg1370: And shalt put away iniquity far from thy tabernacle: the body is taken as the tabernacle of the soul, and the mind as that of the thoughts. And the sense is: if you return to God after your errors, you will be cleansed in thought and in deed.
25_marg1371: He shall give for earth flint: by earth weakness of action is signified, by flint strength, by torrents of gold the teaching of inward brightness. So to those turned to him he gives for earth the flint of sturdy work.
25_interl2780: the one converted becomes strong from weak, and teaching will abound in the mouth of one who lives well
25_marg1372: For flint torrents of gold: because in return for sturdy work he multiplies the teaching of bright preaching.
25_marg1373: And the Almighty shall be against thy enemies: often when we attend to the sacred words we suffer heavily the snares of malignant spirits. And the sense is: when he has driven the malignant spirits from you, the shining talent of the divine word will grow in you.
25_marg1374: Then shalt thou abound in delights in the Almighty: to abound in delights in the Almighty is to be filled, in love of him, with the feasts of sacred Scripture.
25_interl2782: of the heart, by which one may be seen by God
25_marg1375: And shalt lift up thy face to God: to lift the face to God is to raise the heart to search out lofty things.
25_interl2784: who now for your fault does not hear
25_marg1376: And thou shalt pay vows, etc. He who has vowed vows but through weakness cannot pay them, has this done to him as the penalty of sin, that the power is taken away from one who wills the good. But when the fault that stands in the way is wiped off, at once ability follows the vow.
25_interl2785: it is the mark of the weak to judge just the man they see obtain all he asks, which yet God often denies to his own; or he speaks of spiritual things
25_marg1377: Thou shalt decree a thing, and it shall come to thee: a thing is decreed and comes when the virtue sought by desire, with the Lord’s bounty, prospers in effect too.
25_marg1378: And light shall shine in thy ways: for light to shine in the ways of the just is to scatter the signs of their brightness by the wonderful works of the virtues.
25_marg1379: And it shall come to thee: allegorically. The heretics promise the same things to the afflicted if they follow them.
25_marg1380: For he that hath been humbled: because “he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.”
25_marg1381: And he that shall bow down his eyes, etc. So far as it can be detected through the service of the members, the first showing of pride is usually in the eyes.
25_marg1382: The innocent shall be saved: because he who here is forestalled by grace so as to become innocent, when he is brought to judgment, is rewarded for his merit.
25_interl2787: while you promise better things to the converted
25_marg1383: Now also in bitterness: the mind of the just man is always in bitterness, even in prosperity; which bitterness adversity redoubles.
25_marg1384: Whence: “Now also,” as it was in prosperity. Or “now also,” that is, while you promise better things. “Now also my words are in bitterness,” because the effort of a disordered consolation has multiplied the blow it ought to have lessened. For the just groan the more as they see the wicked flatter, who seek to lead astray by sweet words.
25_interl2788: the strength of the blow, because we are not only divided from God, whence we are blind, but also bound in this exile
25_marg1385: And the hand of my scourge: the hand of the scourge is the strength of the blow. But because from adversities the just thirst more for the face of their maker, there follows: “Who will grant me that I might know?” etc. The elect, when they see anything done against their wish, run back to the hidden judgments of God, so as to see in them that what seems to run on in disorder outside is not disposed in disorder within. And this is what he adds: “that I might know” by sight him whom I have known by faith; which he shows he feels, up to: “come even to his throne.”
25_interl2789: which there was even without adversities
25_interl2790: and while I am so weighed down
25_interl2792: in reality as he is; which God now puts off so as to be longed for
25_marg1386: Find him as he is; which God now puts off so as to be longed for more.
25_marg1387: And come even to his throne: the throne is the angels, among whom he longs to be. Or these words fit those placed in this life, because when they see by faith him who presides over the angels, they know that he who wonderfully rules them does not dispose unjustly concerning men; and they condemn their own wishes when they see that God disposes better.
25_interl2793: if I see, then: “I would set”
25_interl2794: namely what we have done, and how terrible the judge is
25_marg1388: Whence: “I would set judgment before him,” etc. To set judgment before God is, within the secret of the mind, through the contemplation of faith, to open the eyes of our consideration to his dread examination: to attend to what sinful man deserves, and to consider how terrible the judge, now hidden and silent, will afterwards appear.
25_marg1389: And would fill my mouth with complaints, etc. Because while he contemplates the judge’s examination against himself, he pursues himself with the bitter invective of penance.
25_marg1390: That I might know the words that he would answer me, etc. For when we pursue our faults by doing penance, we find out what the judge could say to us about them in his examination; which he does not know who neglects his evils.
25_interl2795: but what just man is there, if he examines according to his strength?
25_interl2796: while he shuns his strength, he desires the weakness of the incarnation
25_marg1391: I would not that he should contend with much strength: for who could be found just in the examination if God examined the life of men according to the majesty of his strength? For however just a man is, if he is judged strictly he is crushed by the weight of his greatness. So he adds: “nor overwhelm me with the weight of his greatness,” as if he said: if he contended with me according to his strength, he would crush me with his weight. And note that while he shuns his strength, he desires the weakness of the incarnation.
25_interl2797: however just, if he is judged strictly by the Almighty, he is crushed by the weight of his greatness
25_marg1392: So he adds: “Let him propose equity against me.” The Mediator of God and men is designated by the name of equity, of whom it is written: “who of God is made unto us wisdom and justice.” And the sense is: let him send his incarnate Son to reprove my ways, and then I shall, as victor, shut out the adversary now lying in wait, through the judgment of my acquittal.
25_marg1393: If I go to the east, he appeareth not: as if he said: let him send his Son incarnate. In its height the Godhead could not be grasped, but it showed itself to man through humility. God is not in a part, because he is everywhere, and he is found the less if he is sought in a part. Or: he goes to the east who lifts his mind in consideration of the majesty; but God does not appear to him in his nature. From there the mind, beaten back, returns to itself as to the west, and sees how much remains above it and that it is unworthy to see. To the left, as one who consents to sins, who by no means grasps God. He turns to the right who is lifted up over his virtues, who does not see God. But in all these the soul does not fully know even itself.
25_interl2799: as if: I cannot see him, but he sees me; whence he is to be feared the more
25_marg1394: Whence: “But he knoweth my way,” that is, I cannot see him who sees me.
25_interl2800: he is called just by God before the scourges, but he thinks less of himself, saying that he is being purged there
25_marg1395: And has tried me as gold, etc. He does not compare himself to gold in haughtiness, but considers his own state humbly, as every just man may. And this is: “and has tried me as gold,” etc. For by the burning of tribulation vices are taken away and merits increased.
25_interl2803: his workings: that he helps the good and bears with the wicked; or the examples of the incarnate Word, since he could not see the heights of the hidden disposing
25_marg1396: My foot hath followed his steps: blessed Job was intent on the future working of Wisdom that was to be made flesh; and while, filled with the Spirit from on high, he looked with careful attention on his life, foreseeing the future humility of his gentleness, he ran back to it as to an example set before him.
25_marg1397: I have kept his way: to keep is by intention; not to decline is by working.
25_interl2804: he keeps and does not decline who carries out these things where he intends them
25_marg1398: From the commandments of his lips: the minds of the just stand before almighty God by their intention, and in Scripture they look as it were on his mouth.
25_interl2805: in this he shows that in all the good things he had done he believed himself to be nothing
25_marg1399: And the words of his mouth I have hid in my bosom: we hide the words of his mouth in the bosom of the heart, since we hear his commandments not in passing but to be fulfilled in deed. And if the words come out in deed, yet they lie hidden in the heart if the mind is not lifted up within; but if praise is sought outside, then the word of God is not hidden in the bosom.
25_marg1400: For he is alone, principally and unchangeably. For he alone is of himself, who does all things; in which he himself is to be feared, not the things we suffer. Of his unchangeableness he adds: “and no man can turn away his thought,” because judgments once fixed can by no means be changed.
25_interl2807: as his substance is unchangeable, so also is his will
25_interl2808: and therefore he is to be feared by the weak
25_marg1401: And his soul: that very power by which he disposes all things is called his soul.
25_interl2810: that which seems to resist his will serves him
25_interl2812: as if: even if an evil that is not yet ought to be feared, I, already set in evils, fear others
25_marg1402: When he shall have fulfilled his will in me: he fulfils his will in me, because he afflicts me with many blows. But many like things are at hand with him, because if he thinks to strike, room is still found where the wound may grow.
25_interl2814: because he sets the fear of the majesty before his heart
25_marg1403: And therefore I am troubled at his presence: he is shaken with dread of the uprightness, when he sees he is not fit to give account if he is judged strictly.
25_interl2815: for he who does not consider the force of his punishment does not fear
25_interl2816: nor is this from me, because
25_interl2817: that it may be pierced by fear of the judgment
25_marg1404: God hath softened my heart: so he attributes the virtue of his strength not to himself but to his maker. “Hath troubled me”: the hearts of the just are never secure, but troubled by fear of the judgment; yet they are consoled by the gifts they have received. Whence: “For I have not perished.” The scourges of the just either purge past sins or turn away future ones; which is not so in Job, but his virtue is increased.
25_interl2818: truly God hath softened my heart, and I always fear
25_marg1405: For I have not perished because of the darkness that hangs over me, etc. He, set under the scourge, perishes from bodily health because of the darkness hanging over him, who is struck for past deeds so as to be hidden from the punishments to come.
25_interl2819: even if it sometimes touched it
25_marg1406: Neither hath the mist covered my face, etc. For the mist of sin has not covered the face of his heart who always looked at the weight of the divine strength.
25_interl2820: he curbs himself with the bridle of knowledge, not to be wiser than he ought
25_interl2821: but I cannot comprehend concerning him
25_interl2822: among which we are rolled along
25_marg1407: Times are not hid from the Almighty: because he indeed beholds our times so as to grasp them.
25_interl2823: God is simple in nature, and he and his days are not different. For he has eternity, but he himself is his own eternity. And those who know him still do not know, because him whom we truly believe, yet how his very eternity is we do not know.
25_marg1408: But they that know him, know not, etc. Because even if we now know God by faith, yet how his eternity is, without past or future, we do not see. Blessed Job, bearing witness that the days of the Lord cannot be grasped, lest he be wiser than he ought, soon turns his mind’s regard to the pride of the heretics, who long to be wise in high things.
25_marg1409: Of whom there follows: “Some have removed landmarks.” Whom does he designate by the name of “others” but the heretics, since they stand outside the bosom of holy Church? They remove landmarks, because by transgressing they overstep the decrees of the fathers. They take away flocks by force and feed them, because they draw the unskilled to themselves by perverse persuasions and nourish them with pestilent doctrines for slaughter.
25_marg1410: They have driven away the ass of the fatherless, etc. He calls the fatherless the elect, who are nourished by the great grace of faith and do not yet see the face of their Father, who has already died for them. And there are many who, when they see such men long for heavenly things and hold earthly ones in contempt, supply them with help from the things they possess; such a one is as it were the ass of the elect, who carries burdens for their use. But when the heretics turn such a one away from the Church, they drive away as it were the ass of the fatherless, because when they draw him to faithlessness they drive him from the service of the good.
25_marg1411: And have taken away the widow’s ox for a pledge: the Church is called a widow, being deprived for the meantime of the sight of her slain husband. The ox of this widow is each preacher. And it happens that heretics draw away by perverse doctrines even the preachers themselves. For when a pledge is taken, it is one thing that is held, yet something else is still sought; and so the heretics try to carry off those who preach so as to draw away their followers too.
25_marg1412: So there is added: “They have overturned the way of the poor,” etc. Sometimes those who seem meek and humble fall by the examples of others if they do not know how to keep discretion.
25_marg1413: Others like wild asses, etc. For there are heretics who shrink from mixing with the peoples, but seek the retreat of a more secluded life, and infect the more with the plague of their persuasion as they seem more worthy of reverence from the merits of their life. They are compared to wild asses, who, let loose in their pleasures, are strangers to the bond of faith and reason.
25_marg1414: Go forth to their work, etc. For they carry out not God’s work but their own, while they follow not right doctrines but their own desires.
25_marg1415: By watching for a prey, etc. They watch for a prey who always try to snatch the words of the just to their own sense, so as by this to get the bread of error for their perverse children.
25_interl2828: Scripture, from which heretics take sentences to suit their own senses
25_marg1416: They reap the field that is not their own: by the name of field or vineyard the Church is signified, which perverse preachers reap; and they gather the vintage by oppressing her maker in his members; they who, persecuting the Creator’s grace, when they snatch from her some who seemed upright, what else do they take away but ears of corn or clusters of souls?
25_interl2829: Scripture too, which brings forth clusters of virtues
25_interl2830: they oppress by violence the author of Scripture, whose sense they bend by violence
25_interl2831: because they gather sentences from it for themselves
25_marg1417: They send men away naked, taking away their clothes: as clothes protect the body, so good works protect the soul. So heretics, when they destroy the good works of some, take away their clothes.
25_marg1418: Who have no covering, etc. Covering belongs to justice, cold to fault. So he is cold and covered who by one work glows toward justice and by another grows cold toward fault. But when heretics take good works away from such men, they bring it about that in the cold they have nothing to clothe themselves with. Or cold is evil desire, against which the good cover themselves with the garment of good work; but the wicked bring it about that those who are cold with desire die without the garment of good work.
25_interl2832: the streams of the holy fathers
25_marg1419: Who are wet with the showers of the mountains: that is, whom the streams of the preachers fill.
25_interl2833: when they are mighty in the world
25_marg1420: And having no covering embrace, etc. He calls strong men in the Church, such as the martyrs, stones. So what do they do who trust in no work of their own but run by prayer to the protection of the holy martyrs, except that, because they have no covering of good action, they embrace the stones?
25_interl2834: the tender ones of the Church
25_marg1421: They have violently robbed the fatherless: heretics do violence in robbing, because they rage against the weak minds of the faithful with the violence of words and deeds.
25_marg1422: And stripped the poor common people: because, while they do not prevail over the learned, they strip the unlearned of their covering.
25_marg1423: From the naked and them that go without clothing: he who does neither good nor evil is naked and idle. But he who does evil goes naked, because he goes along the road of wickedness without the covering of good work. From these, when they are hungry and long through penance for the food of the word, the heretics take away the ears of corn, because they destroy in their minds the sayings of the fathers. These are signified by ears of corn, because when sayings are brought forth in figure, we take from them the covering of the letter as the chaff of the beards, so as to be refreshed with the marrow of the spirit.
25_marg1424: They have taken their rest at noon among the stores of them: do those who persecute the Church tread the winepresses? For while the unjust press down the just, they put the clusters under their feet, so that the clusters of souls may flow into spiritual wine, which, stripped of corruptible flesh, run to heavenly things as into a storehouse. But they tread and are thirsty who by doing cruel things become fiercer by that very fact and aim to do heavier things. When the heretics see them do cruel things against the Catholics, they rest at noon among their stores. And they thirst after treading the winepresses, because they join themselves to the multitude of those whom they see do grievous things and thirst for still more grievous ones. And when they cannot stir up persecution by themselves, they rouse the mighty of the world to it; and while their heat satisfies their desires, they rest in their acts as at noon.
25_interl2840: whom they press the harder to put out
25_marg1425: Out of the cities they have made men to groan: because cities are named from peoples living together, by the name of cities churches are designated. But the heretics, clinging to the mighty, persecute the common life of the good. “Out of the cities they have made men to groan,” that is, those who run along the way of God not loosely but manfully.
25_interl2841: because, even if by a just order he permits something unjust to be done unrevenged, yet he does not let the unjust thing which he justly permitted to be done pass away
25_marg1426: And the soul of the wounded hath cried out, etc. The soul of the just is wounded when the faith of the weak is troubled. And it cries out while it pines at another’s fall.
25_marg1427: They have been rebellious to the light: they are rebellious to the light who, following their own desires, despise the good they know.
25_interl2842: they sin not by ignorance but by pride who do not do what they know; whence they are blinded so as not to know what they do not do
25_marg1428: They have not known his ways: for those who are first rebellious knowingly are afterwards blinded so as not to know.
25_marg1429: Neither have they returned, etc. A path is narrower than a way; and because they scorn to do the plainer things, they do not come to understand the subtler ones. God waited for them to go along his paths; but would that they had been willing at least to return by them, so as to hold by penance the roads of life which they would not hold by innocence!
25_interl2843: in these, one is the murderer, another the adulterer
25_marg1430: The murderer riseth at the very break of day, etc. Because every wicked man, in the prosperity of the present life, which is designated by the morning, kills the life of the humble by pressing it down; and placed in adversity and casting down, which is designated by the night, he harms them secretly by wicked counsels, like a thief.
25_interl2844: when prosperity is changed, the same mind remains
25_interl2845: because adultery in the mind is hard to be pierced by human sight, and he does it the more securely as he does not fear to be seen
25_marg1431: The eye of the adulterer observeth darkness, saying: No eye shall see me: this is said of heretics. For as he who commits adultery unlawfully joins to himself the flesh of another’s wife, so heretics, when they snatch a faithful soul into their error, take as it were another’s wife.
25_interl2846: the adulterer, lest he be known
25_marg1432: And he will cover his face: the face of the human heart is the likeness of God. The wicked man covers it so that he cannot be known by the strict judge, when he confounds his life with evil deeds. Whence he will say: “I never knew you.”
25_marg1433: He diggeth through houses in the dark, etc. By the name of houses consciences are designated, in which we dwell when we are dealing with something good. Heretics seek out counsels and wait for the casting down of the just from prosperity, so that in the darkness of adversity, saying that this befalls them for their sins, they may dig through their minds by persuasion; to whom, while they lived prosperously, they did not dare to speak perverse things.
25_interl2848: they contrive to harm them from the adversity of the good
25_marg1434: As in the day they had appointed for themselves: because when they saw the just in prosperity, since they could not speak, they gave themselves to malignant counsels against them.
25_interl2850: the mind of the just man
25_marg1435: If the morning suddenly appear, etc. For when they see the just break forth to the height of ruling power, they are troubled.
25_marg1436: These rejoice at the casting down of the good. But “if the morning suddenly appear,” that is, if the good come to rule, “it is to them the shadow of death,” because they fear to be punished for the things they have done perversely; they will not be corrected, but choose to go loosely and rejoice in fault.
25_marg1437: Whence he says: “and they walk in darkness as if it were in light.” Because they so rejoice in the night of sin as if the light of justice shone round them. Or in their present blindness they are as glad as if they already enjoyed the light of the eternal homeland.
25_marg1438: He is light upon the face of the water: the surface of water is driven hither and thither by the breeze. But the mind of the wicked man is lighter than the surface of water, because whatever breeze of temptation touches it draws it along without the slowness of drawing back. “He is light”: he returns from the plural to the singular, because when one begins evil many imitate; yet the fault is chiefly his who goes before; whence the sentence often returns to him who is the author of the evil.
25_interl2853: the good man, even if he toils, is blessed
25_interl2854: because he is not restrained even by present gifts
25_marg1439: Cursed be: whoever does right in the present life suffers adversity; he is seen indeed to toil in adversity, but he is brought to fulfilment in the blessing of an everlasting inheritance. But whoever does perverse things and yet receives prosperity, and is not restrained from evil deeds even by the bounty of gifts, sees himself prosper indeed, but is bound by the guilt of everlasting cursing.
25_marg1440: Whence it is rightly said now: “Cursed be his portion.” Because even if he is blessed for a time, he is held in the guilt of eternal cursing.
25_marg1441: Let him not walk by the way of the vineyards: he walks by the way of the vineyards who, weighing the preaching of the universal Church, declines neither from the uprightness of faith nor from that of good deeds.
25_marg1442: Let him pass … to excessive heat: iniquity is compared to cold, because it binds the sinner’s mind with numbness. Charity is heat, because it kindles the mind it fills. And there are some who, while they turn from the cold of their iniquities, come to the true faith and to the habit of holiness; yet because, by too much inquiry into the secrets of God, they often slip into error, they pass from the snow waters to excessive heat.
25_marg1443: The unbeliever, or one doing wicked things, is snow water; but when he leaves these things in the faith to which he is led, and longs to search out more than he grasps, that is, to be wiser than he ought, he is hotter than he ought to be. And because he who thinks himself wise is hardly humbled so as to believe those who preach right things, he adds: “and his sin even to hell,” etc. Sin is brought down even to hell which is not amended before the end of life.
25_marg1444: Let mercy forget him: God’s mercy is said to forget him who has forgotten the justice of the Almighty. For whoever does not now fear the just one cannot afterwards find him merciful.
25_marg1445: May worms be his sweetness: because it is the nature of worms to move at every moment, by the name of worms the restlessness of thoughts is signified. So the sweetness of a perverse mind is a worm, because it delights in that by which it is ceaselessly driven through the restlessness of worldly care. The flesh too can be signified by the name of worm, which is the sweetness of the lustful and of anyone given to the flesh. See how blind is he who loves a worm.
25_marg1446: Worms: the corruption of the flesh is expressed. Nothing avails so much for taming the desires of the flesh as to weigh what it is like when dead. For there it is seen that if it is loved, rot and the stench of putrefaction are loved.
25_interl2858: of God, so that God may call him back from iniquity, so that some grace may be given him
25_interl2859: to be broken is to be cut off into Gehenna at death
25_interl2860: which the earth of God fed and the rain watered
25_marg1447: Let him be remembered no more: God looks on the life of the wicked and forgets it, because those whom he judges by the strictness of his sentence he does not know, so far as the memory of mercy goes.
25_interl2862: because there are barren women who afterwards bear
25_marg1448: For he hath fed the barren: in this place the flesh is called barren, which, while it longs only for present things, does not know how to beget good thoughts.
25_marg1449: And to the widow: the soul is called a widow, because her husband suffered death for her and is now hidden from her eyes. Or the preacher of error, while he teaches a people placed outside the unity of the Church, indeed feeds a barren woman who by no means yields spiritual fruits. And he does no good to the widow, because he scorns to serve the Church, whose husband lives in heaven, as though in another place.
25_interl2864: because the proud in the world are easily caught; against which: “God hath chosen the weak things of the world, that he may confound the strong”
25_marg1450: He hath pulled down the strong: in the strength of his wickedness he pulls down the strong when by the cunning of his error he snatches the mighty of this world.
25_interl2866: any wicked man too stands in the Church by faith, and yet is charged with not believing because it is without works
25_interl2867: yet God by a wonderful dispensation, etc.
25_marg1451: And when he standeth up, he shall not trust to his life: the perverse preacher stands in this world so long as he lives in the earthly body; but he refuses to trust to his life, because he scorns to know true things about God.
25_interl2868: because he seeks the things that are his own. Solomon: “The eyes of fools are in the ends of the earth”
25_interl2869: not in the ways of God, but each in his own vice
25_marg1452: His eyes are upon his ways: the sinner looks on his own ways, because he strives to think on and see only the things that serve his temporal advantage.
25_interl2870: because by the very fact that they are lifted up they are far from the true being of God, because it is puffing up, not substance
25_interl2871: because even if it is long here, yet what is ended is short
25_marg1453: They are lifted up for a little while: for those who are divided from the eternal solidity cannot stand.
25_interl2872: and then taken away: “as the tops,” etc.
25_marg1454: And shall be brought down as all things, etc. All earthly things, surely. And the sense is: they can by no means stand, because the very things they lean on flee too; and while they love temporal things, they run through with them by the rolling of time.
25_interl2873: the beards spring up on high, the grains lie hidden lower down; but when the beards are broken, the grains will appear
25_marg1455: And as the tops of the ears of corn, etc. The tops of the ears are the beards. What should I call the wicked rich of this world but certain beards of the human race? They separate themselves from the unity of charity by swelling of mind, and stand stiff like beards; yet they press the grains down in concord; but their stiffness is broken by the strength of the last threshing, and the grains appear.
25_interl2874: the just man, even if he sometimes speaks in sinning, yet it is not fitting that he be judged by the wicked
25_marg1456: And if it be not so, etc. The sense is: all things are as I have set them out; yet even if they were not so, I could by no means be refuted by you, because while you still give way to your own falsehood you cannot reprove another’s; whence we have authority that even if the just man sometimes speaks in sinning, yet it is not fitting that he be judged by the wicked.
25_marg1457: And set my words before God: as if he said: you cannot set what I say before the judge, because by sinning you hide his face from yourselves. He sets false words before God who examines them within himself in the sight of truth, who weighs outward things having considered the inward judge.
25_marg1458: Then Baldad answered, etc. Because Job had said many things against those swollen with these powers, Baldad, profiting from his correction, acknowledges with whom true power lies.
25_marg1459: Saying: “Power and terror are with him, who maketh peace,” etc. He alone truly strikes terror into the hearts of mortals who truly possesses these things from the power of his Godhead. For what terror does human power strike, which does not know when it will lose the right of that same power?
25_marg1460: Who maketh peace: the highest things are set in concord while the lowest are thrown into confusion; and the elect are joined to the angels by the very means by which he lets the reprobate rage against them and oppose them. Though there is the highest peace in the high places, yet in Daniel angels are read to resist angels; not that they disagree among themselves, but the merits of the nations over which they preside do: even if the prophet’s prayer for the deliverance of the people deserves to be heard, the life of that same people, still needing to be purged, speaks against it. And this is not to strive for them, but for the angels justly to examine their deeds; and seeing the will of God, they never will what they cannot obtain.
25_interl2876: of angels or of elect men
25_marg1461: Is there any numbering of his soldiers? The number of the higher spirits is not within human knowledge. They are called soldiers because they fight against the powers of the air, not by toil but by command.
25_interl2877: their virtue is not from themselves but from grace
25_marg1462: And upon whom shall not his light arise? Because the virtue of those same soldiers, or of the elect, is strengthened not by their own powers but by the pouring in of grace from above; which, if it did not arise in our heart, our mind would surely remain in darkness.
25_interl2880: this verse was said above by Job; now it is turned back against him
25_interl2882: even if man had not sinned, he still could not be compared with God; and to him is added the fault of the woman
25_interl2883: no, because not even the highest saints are without fault
25_marg1463: So there is added: “Can man be justified compared with God, or he that is born of a woman appear clean?” Because man is born through a woman made subject to fault, the weakness of the first guilt is passed on in the offspring.
25_interl2884: nor does the Church shine forth with so many miracles by her own power
25_marg1464: Behold even the moon doth not shine, and the stars are not pure, etc. By the moon the Church is designated; by the stars the souls of individual good livers, who long to subdue faults perfectly. But so long as they are bound by the corruption of the flesh, they are tied by its chains. “How much less man that is rottenness.”
25_marg1465: And the son of man who is a worm: as if he said: if those who already live in heavenly desire cannot be free from sin, what weights of sins do they bear who still live fleshly? It must be noted that man is called rottenness, the son of man a worm. For the first man was rottenness, not a worm, because even if he rotted through the flesh, he did not come from rottenness by birth. But the son of man is called a worm, because he is propagated from the corruption of bodies already mortal: as the son of man from man, so the worm is born from rottenness.
25_marg1466: Then Job answered: the words of his friends being ended, Job now at the last rises more sharply against them, as it is the custom of the skilled to keep the stronger things for the conclusion.
25_interl2887: Yet the mighty one himself is helped, as Paul says, but humbly; not so that they presume upon their own sense, reckoning themselves useful to God.
25_marg1467: Whose helper art thou? is it of him that is weak? and dost thou hold up? To help the weak belongs to charity; to want to help the mighty belongs to haughtiness. And the sense is: while you aim to help him under whose greatness you sink, the comfort you give comes from display, not from devotion.
25_marg1468: To whom hast thou given counsel? To give counsel to a fool belongs to charity; to give counsel to Wisdom itself belongs to perversity.
25_marg1469: Whence there follows: “and thou hast shewn thy very great prudence,” etc. Everyone whose prudence is right does not have very great prudence, because he does not long to be wiser than he ought.
25_marg1470: Very great: beyond measure, as those who long to seem more learned than others; whence it happens that the immoderate speak even foolish things. So there is added, on the excess of prudence: “Whom hast thou desired to teach? was it not him?” etc. We live by the breath of life, without which we are not wise, but through which we are; “so he who gives life gives wisdom too.”
25_interl2889: as if you were wiser than he from whom you have your living
25_interl2890: that is, the spirit of living life
25_marg1471: Was it not him that made life? Baldad, because he believed Job was scourged for fault, was seen to pry with proud rashness into the hidden judgment of God, which he ought humbly to have revered. So he set himself above him in prudence whose judgment he judged without understanding it. But because Job, bearing the figure of the Church, brought forth a few things for the correction of the proud, he suddenly opens out into teaching through sentences, saying: “life.”
25_marg1472: Augustine: as we can, not from our own nature by which we are men, but from this air poured round us, which we draw in and let out by breathing and breathing again, make a breath when we blow, so the Almighty, not from his own nature nor from the underlying creature, but even from nothing, could make the breath which, by putting it into the body of man, he is most fittingly said to have breathed or blown in: the incorporeal an incorporeal thing, but the unchangeable a changeable one, because the uncreated a created one.
25_marg1473: Life: after he has checked the swelling, he teaches wisdom, as if: why is man proud of knowledge, when the abyss of ignorance weighs down even the proud angels?
25_marg1474: Behold the giants groan under the waters: the giants are the proud, the waters are the peoples. For the haughty, while in this world they long to reach the honour of loftiness, groan under the weights of the peoples; and each man is set under those peoples in mind over whom he is set in dignity. And by these words it is shown that all pride lies at the bottom by the very fact that it raises itself on high.
25_marg1475: And they that dwell with them: those who are joined to such men groan likewise, because they too are pressed down by sharing in their toil; and because the loftinesses desired cannot be administered without sins, and the evil that is done is not hidden from the divine anger.
25_marg1476: There follows: “Hell is naked before him, and there is no covering for destruction.” By the name of hell and destruction he designates the devil and all the companions of his damnation.
25_interl2892: the Jews are subject to the devil
25_interl2893: but because grace fills even the empty:
25_marg1477: He stretched out the north over: by the name of the north the devil is called, who, to bind the hearts of the nations with the cold of numbness, said: “I will sit in the mountain of the covenant, in the sides of the north.” He is stretched out over the empty space, because he possesses those hearts which are not possessed by the grace of divine love.
25_interl2894: he founds the Church upon the nations; but in what order? This:
25_marg1478: And hangeth the earth upon nothing: by the name of earth the Church is designated, which yields the fruits of good work. By nothing, the gentile peoples. The earth is hung on nothing which before was held empty by the north, because those hearts of the gentiles were filled with the charity of God which before had been pressed down by the numbness of the devil. Or by the empty space the unbelief of Judea is designated; by nothing, the nations, of whom it is said by the prophet: “All nations are before him as if they had no being at all, and are counted to him as nothing, and vanity.”
25_interl2896: but something is kept for the perfect
25_marg1479: He bindeth up the waters in his clouds, so that they break not out and fall down together: he tells of the beginnings of the Church being born, saying that God tempers the preaching of the teachers, so that the weakness of the hearers, nourished by the dew of the teachers, may grow strong. For if they poured out knowledge with the mouth as they drank it in with the heart, they would crush the hearers with its immensity.
25_interl2898: so the preacher does not pour out below all that he knows, just as God does not show him all the things above
25_interl2899: because we are clouded by the darkness of our ignorance from seeing it
25_interl2900: whence: “darkness was under his feet,” because he is not seen by those below with the brightness with which he rules among those above
25_marg1480: The face of his throne: the throne is his majesty, or the angels, who cannot now be fully known. Or we ourselves, whose face, that is, knowledge, is forbidden to advance to higher things; over whom is the cloud in which he puts forth hidden judgments. So he adds: “He hath set bounds.”
25_marg1481: He withholdeth the face of his throne, etc. In the face, knowledge is shown. So the face of his throne is withheld, because the glory of his kingdom is not known by us in this life. A cloud is said to be spread over it, because that heavenly glory is not seen as it is.
25_interl2902: until the courses of the just and the unjust are ended
25_marg1482: He hath set bounds about the waters, till light and darkness come to an end: because he moderates the knowledge of the human race, so that so long as the changes of alternating times pass by, they do not perfectly reach the knowledge of the inward brightness.
25_interl2903: no wonder if the fleshly do not know heavenly things, since those on whom the spiritual building rises
25_interl2905: not with penal fear, but with wonder
25_marg1483: The pillars of heaven tremble, and dread at, etc. He calls the holy angels, or the highest preachers of the Church, the pillars of heaven.
25_interl2908: but how? He conquered not by force but by reason, in that God became man to be sacrificed for sins and to set free justly
25_marg1484: By his power the seas are suddenly gathered together: because when the Lord became flesh, the discordant hearts of the churches believe in concord.
25_marg1485: And his wisdom has struck the proud one: the ancient enemy was struck by wisdom, not by force, because while he once boldly attacked Christ, in whom nothing belonged to him, he lost by right the man whom he also held justly. But, the Lord being slain, what the glory of the preachers would be follows.
25_marg1486: There follows: “His spirit hath adorned the heavens,” because the preachers, unless they had received the promised gifts of the Paraclete, would have shone with no beauty of strength.
25_interl2911: from the hearts in which he had rested
25_marg1487: And his obstetric hand brought forth the winding serpent, etc. The ancient enemy, who spoke to man by the mouth of a serpent; who is called winding because he did not stand in the uprightness of truth. He was cast out from the Church by the Lord’s obstetric hand. In a few sentences he has related the order of the Lord’s first coming; but he adds that the second is greatly to be feared.
25_marg1488: Lo, these things are said in part of his ways, etc. By the name of ways he calls the Lord’s actions, telling of the Lord’s coming as the ways of the Lord. He spoke in part, because one action of his was that by which he made us, another that by which he redeemed us. That he calls it a little drop of his words is because whatever high thing we, set in this life, know from the consideration of him flows to us like a thin drop of the liquid from above.
25_marg1489: And seeing we have heard scarce a little drop of his word, who shall be able to behold the thunder of his greatness? As if he said: if we scarcely bear the wonders of his humility, by what strength shall we endure the terrible coming of his majesty?
25_interl2913: while speaking of the word of God and the greatness of the thunder; as if: since it is so, I will not yield to words or scourges or swords
25_marg1490: Added: how mystically this man’s sayings are uttered is shown when he is said to take up a parable, that is, a likeness, lest we weigh his words only according to the text; because he both tells of his own things and signifies the times of holy Church afflicted.
25_marg1491: Job also added: the Church suffers bitter things from her enemies in two ways: by words, where her wisdom is exercised, or by swords, where her patience is proved. Now he speaks of that persecution in which she is assailed by false assertions.
25_interl2914: calling on the life of God he binds himself to what he adds, namely: “as long as”
25_marg1492: As God liveth: there are those who, suffering adversity, do not believe that God exists; some reckon that God exists but does not care at all for human affairs. This man, set in the figure of the Church in affliction, says, so as to confess that God exists: “As God liveth.” And to declare that he cares for human affairs he adds: “who hath taken away my judgment,” etc.
25_interl2915: for he thinks he suffers not by chance but by God’s disposing
25_interl2916: to cling perfectly to the truth, he declares that he will not lie either by design or by haste
25_interl2918: having answered that he does not lie, he adds in what things he agrees with the truth, saying
25_marg1493: My lips shall not speak iniquity, etc. That he says iniquity first and lying afterwards is because all iniquity is a lie, as it is out of tune with God’s equity and truth; but it is worse to contrive a lie than to speak one. For speaking is mostly a matter of haste, contriving of studied wickedness.
25_marg1494: God forbid that I should judge you to be just: because Solomon says: “He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, both are abominable before God.” And this is: “God forbid,” etc. For he would depart from innocence if he reckoned the wicked good.
25_marg1495: My justification: he would forsake the justification he had begun if he turned aside to the praise of sinners.
25_marg1496: My justification: he rightly keeps off from others’ sins who first guards himself from his own; as if: I fear to sin in this because my heart does not reprehend me.
25_interl2922: when anyone reads or hears the good things he has despised, his conscience reproves him heavily
25_marg1497: For my heart doth not reprehend me: as if he said: I ought not to be dragged into fault for your sake, I who have dreaded to sin in my own concerns. But how does he deny that he is reprehended by his heart, who says above: “I have sinned”? He sinned indeed, or in thought; but he does not confess that he is reprehended by his heart, because even if in thinking unlawful things he fell short of uprightness, yet he resisted the thought strongly.
25_interl2925: truly wicked, even if he seems just
25_marg1498: Let my enemy be as the ungodly: the ungodly is the unbeliever; the wicked is he who by perversity of work is out of tune with equity. So the Church has enemies among the ungodly outside, and suffers the wicked within. And “as” and “like” stand for affirmation. But if they are said for likeness, he marks the fleshly whom she suffers within by their likeness to the ungodly; as if he said: he who does not agree with me in work differs from me in faith too.
25_interl2926: in the future, since here he seeks all
25_marg1499: For what is the hope of the hypocrite: the hypocrite, who in Latin is called a pretender, is a covetous robber, who, while doing wickedly and longing to be revered for holiness, robs the praise of another’s life.
25_interl2927: as if: he will not be heard by God in the time of distress, because in the time of peace he did not hear God
25_marg1500: Will God hear his cry? Because in the judgment he finds no remedy in crying who now loses the fitting time for crying. Of whose perversity it is added: “Or can he delight himself in the Almighty?” etc. He who is overcome by love of earthly things by no means delights in God.
25_interl2928: he who loves the world, the charity of the Father is not in him; and if he does not love, he does not call upon him
25_marg1501: And call upon God at all times: the hypocrite calls upon God only when tribulation in earthly things straitens him.
25_interl2929: having so far rooted out evil things, he plants right ones
25_interl2930: as if: you are not wise for this reason, that you give it not to the hand of God but to yourselves
25_interl2931: he teaches in such a way as to hide nothing of the truth which it profits to know
25_marg1502: I will teach you by the hand: the Son is called the hand of God: “For all things were made by him.” And the sense is: of myself I know nothing; but whatever I perceive of the truth, I grasp by the bounty of that same truth.
25_interl2932: as if: even if you know anything, it is to your judgment
25_marg1503: Behold you all know it: “To him therefore who knoweth to do good, and doth it not, to him it is sin.”
25_interl2933: who, even if they have it from themselves to act wickedly, yet it belongs to God to judge these things justly
25_marg1504: This is the portion of a wicked man, etc. The heretics are called ungodly, who through error are strangers to the knowledge of truth. He also calls them violent, because they try by violence to bend sacred Scripture to a perverse understanding.
25_marg1505: If his sons be multiplied: those who are begotten by the preaching of heretics are struck by the sentence of the judgment to come.
25_marg1506: And his grandsons shall not be filled with bread, etc. The grandsons of the heretics are those who are born from the preaching of the erring sons. Whom bread never fills, because while in the food of the sacred word they seek more than they grasp, they are always fasting from the knowledge of truth. But because the Church gathers some from the heretics, she leaves some stubborn in malice.
25_marg1507: There follows: “They that shall remain of him,” namely of that people of the heretics, “shall be buried in death,” because while they do not return to the light of truth, they are pressed down by earthly understanding.
25_interl2936: or: the widows remaining in error, while they reckon that their preacher was holy, do not mourn, by a false hope
25_interl2937: by whose death they would seem bound to be afflicted
25_marg1508: And his widows shall not weep: he calls widows the subject peoples left destitute by the heretic’s death; who, when the preacher of error is snatched off to eternal torments, often return to the grace of true knowledge.
25_marg1509: If he shall heap together silver as earth: silver, that is, the eloquence of the heretics, is compared to earth, because they labour to know something of sacred Scripture out of longing for earthly praise. They also prepare raiment as clay, because they weave in loosely and defilingly the testimonies of sacred Scripture with which they want to defend themselves.
25_marg1510: He shall prepare indeed, but the just man shall be clothed with it: because the man full of right faith gathers the testimonies of Scripture which the heretic brings forward, and from them refutes the stubbornness of error, as David killed Goliath with his own sword.
25_marg1511: And the innocent shall divide the silver: for the innocent to divide the silver is to expound the words of God minutely and with discernment, and to fit to each one what worthily suits him. Or the innocent divides the silver, that is, distinguishes which things the heretics have said soundly and which pestilently, because they mix false things with true.
25_marg1512: He hath built his house as a moth: the moth builds its house by corrupting; so too the heretic makes a place for his faithlessness only in the minds he corrupts.
25_marg1513: And as a keeper he hath made a booth: the keeper’s booth is made firm on no foundation, but is soon destroyed as time passes; so the rest promised by the heretics is destroyed with time, and is by no means found after this life. But because heretics are often propped up by the patronage of the mighty, the discourse rises from the particular destruction of the heretics to a general sentence on the haughty.
25_marg1514: The rich man when he shall sleep, etc. The rich man sleeps and opens his eyes, because when he dies in the flesh his soul is forced to see what it scorned to provide for.
25_interl2942: of the things he held in a dream
25_interl2943: because his soul will be tormented in the lake of hell
25_marg1515: Poverty like water shall take hold on him: for, poverty driving him, the burning rich man was compelled in hell to beg even for the least things, who here, avarice driving him, went so far as to refuse even the least.
25_interl2944: because while he does not know it, the whirlwind of judgment snatches him
25_marg1516: A tempest shall oppress him in the night: he calls the hidden time of a sudden end night; by the name of tempest he designates the whirlwind of judgment.
25_marg1517: A burning wind shall take him up: the malignant spirit is called a burning wind, who snatches off afterwards to the flames of Gehenna him whom he now sets on fire with the fire of perverse lust.
25_marg1518: And as a whirlwind shall snatch him from his place: the place of the perverse is the delight of temporal life.
25_marg1519: And he shall cast upon him, and shall not spare: whenever God corrects the sinner by striking, he sends the scourge so as to spare. But when by striking he closes his life as it remains in sin, he sends the scourge but by no means spares.
25_interl2946: he flees from the hand of God striking who corrects himself; or from the wicked work of the one struck
25_marg1520: Out of his hand he would willingly flee: because the hand is understood as working, he flees from the hand of the one struck, because when he sees the destruction of the wicked man he also leaves the ways of wickedness.
25_interl2947: seeing the punishment of the ungodly he tightens his loosened works
25_marg1521: So there follows: “He shall clasp his hands upon him.” To clasp the hands is to confirm the works of life in uprightness, by seeing in another’s punishment what to fear.
25_interl2948: he will wonder, or will now preach what he did not believe while the ungodly man flourished
25_marg1522: And shall hiss at him, beholding his place: in hissing the intensity of wonder is expressed.
25_interl2951: he is not a debtor set free who has paid back much, but he who has paid back all
25_interl2952: which the eloquence of the proud does not have, or of those who invent new things
25_marg1523: Silver hath beginnings of its veins: after he has sufficiently set out the punishments of the proud mighty, he turns his words back to the heretics. As if he said: whoever prepares himself for the words of true preaching must take the origins of his cases from the sacred pages, which are to us, for speaking, as it were certain veins of silver, because from them we draw the origin of our speech. But the heretics are so proud of the brilliance of their eloquence that they give themselves to no authority of the sacred books at all.
25_marg1524: And gold hath a place wherein it is melted: in this place the heretics are rebuked for their foolish suffering. For they often suffer much for Christ, and hope to become martyrs by these sufferings. Of whom Paul says: “If I should deliver my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing.” So because true martyrs are made only in the Catholic Church, it is rightly said: “gold hath a place wherein it is melted”; as if: true wisdom has a place in which the tribulation of the wicked is purged; because the soul will not shine in the brightness of eternal beauty unless, so to speak, it has first burned here in the workshop of charity.
25_interl2953: but even if it was earth before, now it is strong and sharp for defending. Even if it was hard and senseless before, melted by the fire of God it is changed into true strength
25_marg1525: Iron is taken out of the earth: because stronger men are separated from the earthly action which they held before, and become champions of the Church.
25_marg1526: And stone melted with heat is turned into brass: because a heart hard and cold toward the love of the divine fire is touched by the glow of the Spirit. By that ardour it is both softened toward love and made solid for working, so that as it was hard before in love of the world, so afterwards it may put itself forth in love of God.
25_marg1527: He hath set a time for darkness: that is, for the wicked, a limit at which they cease to be wicked.
25_interl2954: of the elect and of the reprobate
25_marg1528: And the end of all things he considereth: because he looks on the end of the elect, at which they are changed from evil to good. He looks also on the end of the reprobate, at which they are dragged from evil work to punishment. He saw the end of the gentiles, that at some time they would shine with the light of faith; he saw also the end of Judea, that she would blind herself with the darkness of hardened faithlessness.
25_interl2955: that is, those whom now either unbelief blinds or cruelty hardens, the river of flames will separate from the people of the elect; or now preaching forsakes them and turns to the humble
25_marg1529: So there is added: “the stone also that is in the dark,” etc. The people of the Jews, hard with faithlessness, who would not see the author of life whom they had foretold by prophecy, was a stone in the dark, which stood out both hard in cruelty and clouded in unbelief. It is also called the shadow of death, that is, of the devil, because following his iniquity it expressed his image in itself. By the name of the flood is called the fire going out from the sight of the judge at the examination, dividing the elect and the reprobate. Whence the prophet: “A swift stream of fire issued forth from before him.” The people on their journey is the whole number of the elect, who, reckoning this life their exile, sigh for the homeland above with all the intention of their heart. Or by the name of the flood the watering of holy preaching can be understood.
25_marg1530: Those whom … hath forgotten, etc. That is, the Jews, whom the feet and preachers of the Lord, poor according to his humanity, left for the swelling of their pride. And they forgot them when they transferred the seeds of their preaching to bear fruit among the gentiles alone. He calls them such as cannot be come at, because they would not give the words of life a way to the heart.
25_interl2957: here he adds what Judea was like before, or what she has now suffered
25_marg1531: The land, out of which bread grew: because Judea both had first the law to refresh her, and afterwards, having seen the Redeemer’s miracles, the envy that burned her up.
25_interl2958: the place is pride, from which envy is usually born; that is, it burned with envy because pride did not let go
25_interl2959: he describes her further; the following fault is increased by the preceding glory
25_interl2960: stones: the minds of the strong
25_marg1532: The stones of it are the place of sapphires: sapphires are of the colour of the sky. And he says this because holy souls leading a heavenly life were never lacking from Judea.
25_marg1533: And the clods of it are gold: he calls clods the gatherings of the several orders of prophets and teachers, who by the great pouring in of grace held themselves together in unanimity of profession and work. For clods are bound together from moisture and dust. And those are called gold who shone with virtue of life and wisdom. But why she lost these goods follows: “The bird hath not known the path.” In this place by the name of bird he is signified who, ascending to the heavens, poised there the fleshly body he had taken. Judea did not know the bird’s path, because she would not consider the ways of Christ’s humility by which he raised us to high things.
25_interl2962: humility, which raises to high things
25_interl2963: the intention of the death by which he re-forms us
25_interl2964: the vulture, while it flies, if it sees a carcass, lets itself down to it; so the Son of God
25_marg1534: Neither hath the eye of the vulture beheld it: our Redeemer is designated by the name of vulture, who, remaining in the height of his Godhead, as by a lofty flight caught sight of the carcass of our mortality in the lowest places, and brought himself down from heavenly things to the lowest. And while he sought a dead creature, he found death among us. But the eye of this vulture was the intention of our resurrection. So that people saw the vulture indeed, but did not look at the vulture’s eyes. Whence it also drove back his preachers, of whom it is added: “The children of the merchants have not trodden it.” The merchants are those who carry on spiritual business, who offer preaching to their hearers so as to receive from them faith and right works. These were the prophets, whose children are called the apostles, who would have trodden Judea if they had pressed down her vices with the heel of virtue. Or we take the merchants as the preachers of holy Church, the children of the merchants as pastors and teachers.
25_interl2965: the teachers cease from calling her who drove back the fathers, the apostles
25_marg1535: Neither hath the lioness passed by it: the Church is called a lioness, because by the mouth of holy preaching she kills those who live badly in vices. Whence it is said to Peter: “Kill and eat.” So the Church passed into Judea but did not pass through it, because she snatched a few from it to the faith, yet did not utterly put out the unbelieving people from its faithlessness. But, driven back by the Jews, what did she do? “He hath stretched forth his hand to the flint,” because she sent the arm of her preaching to the hardness of the gentiles.
25_interl2969: because those whom he drains of earthly things he waters with heavenly
25_marg1536: He hath overturned mountains from the roots: the roots are the inmost thoughts of the proud. The mountains were overturned from the roots, because the powers of the world fell from their inmost thought to worship God.
25_interl2970: from hard things the rivers of preaching flow out
25_marg1537: In the rocks he hath cut out rivers: that is, in the hard hearts of the gentiles he opened up rivers of preaching.
25_interl2971: he who is despised by himself is great to God
25_marg1538: And his eye hath seen every precious thing: God saw a precious thing when he looked on human nature, cast down in its own eyes, with the illumination of his wisdom’s grace.
25_marg1539: The depths also of rivers he hath searched: the Lord searches the depths of rivers and brings hidden things into the light, because by his gift spiritual exposition now lights up the dark sayings of the ancients. But because the sayings of God are not pierced without his wisdom, he adds, about searching out those same words: “But where is wisdom to be found?” He set out two things and added two in reply, not solving but increasing what he puts forward. He sets out two things, about the place and about the price. It is plain that not even man’s wisdom can be held by a place or bought with things. Yet he speaks mystically not of created but of creating Wisdom. Otherwise how could he say lower down, after gold, which is dearer, that crystal cannot equal it, as if for immense praise? So he speaks not solving but increasing what he had put forward. And he says Wisdom: “Christ, the power of God, and the wisdom of God.” Man does not know its price, because he finds no worthy merit of work by which to obtain it. For we have been redeemed by grace, and by no merit of ours did the Wisdom of God come to us.
25_interl2975: for the mind which understands these things speaks justly
25_interl2976: it is not said that there is a price and it is not known, but that it is not known because there is none
25_interl2977: for if they were truly wise, they would rather mourn in this exile
25_marg1540: Neither is it found in the land of them that live in delights: he calls the human soul land. This wisdom cannot be found in the land of those who live in delights, because whoever is still fed by the pleasures of this life is separated from the understanding of eternal wisdom.
25_interl2978: he looks back to what he said above: “But where is wisdom,” etc.
25_interl2979: he does not say where wisdom is, but where it is not
25_marg1541: The depth saith: It is not in me: he calls the depth the hearts of men, which are both fluid through falling and dark through the mist of doubleness. Which depth surely confesses that this wisdom is not in it, because the wicked mind, while it longs to be wise in a fleshly way, shows itself foolish toward spiritual things.
25_marg1542: The depth: the wisdom of the world, which is foolishness with God. “Saith” by its very works.
25_marg1543: The sea: the minds of the restless. Israel has the sabbath, Egypt the flies, that is, restlessness. And the sea says: “It is not.” For no one fully receives it except one who strives to draw himself away from all the tossing of fleshly actions. And the troubled minds of worldly men cry out by that very fact that they are far from true wisdom, in that they are not at rest; because this Wisdom of God was to be made flesh, so that to redeem the human race he would send neither holy angels nor holy men, but would come through himself.
25_interl2980: he looks back to what he said: “Man knoweth not the price,” etc.
25_interl2981: he does not say what its price is, but what it is not
25_marg1544: There follows: “The finest gold shall not purchase it.” The holy angels are called the finest gold, who, continuing in the innocence in which they were created, both shine with the brightness of justice and are stained by no filth of fault. But none of them was sent for our redemption.
25_marg1545: The finest gold shall not purchase it: men can be gold, but not the finest, because they shine, but not without the infection of fault.
25_interl2982: nor is Moses the author of salvation, who judges evils but does not heal them
25_marg1546: Neither shall silver be weighed in exchange for it: because the life of just men preaching, or writing the words of God, however strong in the light of holiness, does not convey to us by its presence the coming of the Wisdom from above.
25_interl2983: but neither does uprightness of life from the philosophers suffice
25_marg1547: It shall not be compared with the dyed colours of India: by India this world is taken here, in which the life of men is begotten dark through fault. The dyed colours of India are the wise men of this world, who, at first foul through unbelief and mostly through action, are darkened before human eyes with the colour of an uprightness laid over them; and since they lack the virtue of things, they pretend by the arrangement of their words, as by colours laid over, to be other than they are; from these the Wisdom of God stands far off. The commandments of God please without eloquence, like a garment without dye.
25_interl2984: nor are these the most precious stones, but he chose these to signify something else mystically
25_marg1548: Or with the most precious stone sardonyx, or the sapphire: the sardonyx has the likeness of red earth, the sapphire an airy look. So by the sardonyx are taken men, or the fathers of the Old Testament, following certain earthly things; by the sapphire the preachers of the New Testament, seeking heavenly things alone; or the angels.
25_marg1549: Gold or crystal cannot equal it: after it has been said that gold is not compared to this wisdom, it is further added, as if rising, that not even crystal can equal it; which does not hold according to the letter. In crystal any liquid is shown outside such as it is held within. By gold and crystal we take the fellowship of the saints in the homeland above, who will shine with the brightness of blessedness, and the bulk of the members will not hide the mind of each from the eyes of another. Who, even if they will be like him because they will become blessed, yet are not equal because they are creatures.
25_marg1550: Neither shall any vessels be changed for it: a high vessel of gold: Elias and John and Jeremias. But whoever believed any of them to be the Christ exchanged a high and eminent vessel of gold for Wisdom; because the Church believes Christ not one of the prophets but the Lord of the prophets.
25_interl2987: because those are of themselves, these of him
25_marg1551: Shall not be mentioned in comparison of it: for what are men compared with God? Nothing.
25_interl2988: because: “thou knowest not whence he cometh, and whither he goeth”
25_marg1552: But wisdom is drawn out of secret places: because, since it is invisible, it is found only invisibly. It is said to be drawn because, as we draw breath that the body may live, so the spirit of wisdom is drawn from inmost places that the soul may stand in life. And rightly “out of secret places,” because this wisdom is poured hiddenly into hearts, as it is said of the Spirit: “and thou knowest not whence he cometh, and whither he goeth.”
25_interl2990: man converted from the blackness of sins
25_marg1553: The topaz shall not be equal to it: because it gleams with every colour, the topaz is called as it were “topandion.” And the sense is: none of the saints, though full of every virtue, yet gathered from this blackness of the world, can be equal to it.
25_marg1554: And see that whereas before he had set it above the angels, the ancient fathers, the holy philosophers, the glorified prophets, now in this place he rebukes specially the heretics, who make men converted from sins equal to the God-man, since these are sons by grace, he by nature; which he shows when he adds: “neither shall it be compared to the cleanest dyeing.” They are the cleanest dyeing who humbly keep the grace of the virtues that has come upon them. For they would not be dyed if they had had holiness by nature.
25_interl2991: above he called the colours of India not clean
25_interl2992: baptism is called a dyeing, where the foul are made comely
25_interl2993: it comes from him from whom it sprang
25_marg1555: Whence then cometh wisdom? Because it is born of the invisible Father, its way is hidden. Whence the prophet: “Who shall declare his generation?” And the place of its understanding is the human mind.
